note: This is a planned test inventory; all cases start NOT_RUN, not asserted passing. Keep honest status and actual evidence externally in test runs.

cases.requirement: Loopback static server serves index.html and local CSS/JS; no /api/login or /api/jobs backend.
Record exact real-worktree v86 JS/WASM/BIOS/kernel/initrd/root hashes or mark missing.
Run present geometry tests against disposable Chromium and distinguish historical results.
No modifications to distro ISO pipeline, host package config or public network listeners.
First load shows Username, Password, ANON, SIGNIN, not a fake ready terminal.
ANON with blank username immediately creates a nonempty randomized in-RAM name.
ANON with supplied username renders that name with textContent; HTML/script input not executed.
ANON never requires password, does not inspect it, clears password field if populated.
Two sequential anonymous entries yield distinct session IDs.
ANON action creates no IndexedDB account record, OPFS guest files, or localStorage session data.
Logout clears current browser session, terminal buffer and username/password fields.
Repeated rapid ANON clicks cause one session and one guest launch, not duplicate instances.
Existing menu, window drag, resize, minimize, workspaces and preset import/export remain functional.
Bundled v86 JS/WASM/BIOS assets are served from local origin without CDN.
Browser constructs and runs exactly one actual pinned v86 instance per session.
An actual Debian i386 kernel boots inside Chromium to a working serial shell.
Guest serial uname and id commands return real guest output, not canned strings.
Guest Python arithmetic command yields expected answer through serial I/O.
Guest python3 sqlite3 module imports and reports version through serial I/O.
Guest compiles and executes a small C program or reports missing GCC honestly.
Missing WASM/BIOS/kernel/manifest produces visible failure with an actionable diagnostic, no fake ready prompt.
Static web server serves artifacts but executes no v86 guest commands; browser resource use is observed.
Keyboard/enter typed into real terminal reaches guest serial port; output returns to DOM.
Terminal output survives window close/reopen/minimize without rebooting guest.
Resize, preset switch and compare/reference rendering preserve the one v86 instance.
Rerender does not duplicate serial listeners or send a key twice.
Guest reads sessionId, kind and sanitized displayName from actual guest-visible 9p file.
Guest-visible metadata contains no password, private key, local auth token or host path grant.
Guest writes a unique file and reads it back during the same anonymous session.
After logout and a new anon session the previous file and guest metadata are gone.
After page reload anonymous guest state is gone and no guest write appears in browser persistent stores.
Guest cannot access arbitrary host filesystem files or obtain raw host privileged handle via 9p.
Logout during boot destroys or cancels the guest; no stale ready callback opens previous session.
Unknown normalized local username + acceptable password automatically creates local encrypted identity and starts guest.
UI clearly reports creation is browser-local, not synced and not global account registration.
Known username + correct password after reload unlocks same public-key fingerprint.
Known username + wrong password fails, creates no guest and does not overwrite record.
Password never stored or logged in plaintext, and never transmitted over HTTP/WebRTC/into guest.
Local record has unique salt, AES-GCM IV, ciphertext, SPKI, version and >=600k PBKDF2-SHA256 iterations.
Private signing key encrypted at rest, decrypts/imports on unlock and correctly signs a challenge.
Corrupt AES-GCM ciphertext and malformed KDF metadata reject without account overwrite or guest boot.
Case folding and username normalization produce one canonical local account key.
A clean browser profile does not inherit the first profile account and can create same username independently.
Two-tab concurrent creation cannot overwrite a previously committed account record.
Local usernames admin, owner, root or host username confer no server role or host file rights.
Registered identity uses same v86 controller, ephemeral guest FS and guest command flow as ANON.
Logout releases active credential references; no credential included in public session descriptor.
Existing geometry/multi-workspace browser regression tests pass after real terminal integration.
Docs accurately distinguish implemented features, not-run features and limits.
No application backend, P2P signaling service, runtime CDN or public listener introduced in phase 0.
No accidental /api calls to the static server from ANON/SIGNIN guest path.
Report exact browser, OS, asset hashes, guest console transcript and acceptance ID statuses.
No host filesystem or Linux UID credentials have been exposed to either mode.
